label: Brisnik HR-F1
title: SSRI or SNRI with one bleeding-risk medicine and no stomach protection, age 65 or over
statement: Prescribed SSRI or SNRI - and the patient is aged ≥ 65 years and co-prescribed a single of the following without GI protection: antiplatelet, anticoagulant, and NSAID

source.document: Brisnik V, et al. Deprescribing of antidepressants: indicators of high-risk and overprescribing. BMC Med 2024;22:193, Tables 3-4

plain_summary: An SSRI or SNRI taken with an antiplatelet, a blood thinner or an NSAID raises the risk of bleeding from the stomach or bowel in a person aged 65 or over, and more so when no stomach protection is taken.

medicine_groups.name: SSRIs (selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors)
medicine_groups.note: Generic packs that show the ingredient name with a company name count too. Any dose counts.

medicine_groups.name: SNRIs (serotonin and noradrenaline reuptake inhibitors)
medicine_groups.note: Generic packs that show the ingredient name with a company name count too. Any dose counts.

medicine_groups.name: Antiplatelet medicines
medicine_groups.note: Count aspirin here when the recorded purpose or directions show clot prevention. Cartia and Astrix are low-dose aspirin. A brand identifies aspirin, but the prescribed use decides its group. Aspirin bought over the counter does not appear in a dispensing history. Asasantin SR is aspirin with dipyridamole. CoPlavix and DuoCover each contain aspirin and clopidogrel. Both ingredients belong to Group C.

medicine_groups.name: Anticoagulants (blood thinners)
medicine_groups.note: No Australian brand is listed for edoxaban. Enoxaparin, dalteparin and fondaparinux are injections. Generic packs that show the ingredient name with a company name count too. Count systemic heparin sodium and nadroparin calcium. Exclude heparin used only to flush a catheter.

medicine_groups.name: NSAIDs, the anti-inflammatory pain medicines

ibuprofen: Advil Childrens Pain and Fever 2 to 7 Years
Advil Childrens Pain and Fever 7 to 12 Years
Advil Childrens Pain and Fever Relief 2 to 12 Years
Advil Infants Pain and Fever Relief 3 Months to 2 Years
Nurofen for Children 3 Months to 5 Years

medicine_groups.note: Tablets, capsules, liquids, suppositories and injections count. Skin gels, creams and eye drops do not count. Count systemic aspirin here when the recorded purpose or directions show use for pain or inflammation. Count each aspirin supply once across Groups C and E. Nurofen Plus and Panafen Plus are ibuprofen with codeine. Nuromol and Maxigesic are ibuprofen with paracetamol. Arthrotec (diclofenac with misoprostol) and Vimovo (naproxen with esomeprazole) carry their own stomach protection.

medicine_groups.name: Stomach protection (proton pump inhibitors and misoprostol)
medicine_groups.note: The source does not define 'GI protection'. This working list holds proton pump inhibitors and misoprostol. Whether H2 blockers (for example famotidine) count is for the pharmacist to decide. Exclude Angusta and Gymiso from stomach protection even when their ingredient is recorded as misoprostol. If the use of an unidentified misoprostol product is unclear, ask which product was used and why before counting it as protection.

rule_for_models: At age 65 or over, flag a Group A SSRI or Group B SNRI with exactly one of Group C (antiplatelet), D (anticoagulant) or E (systemic NSAID) when the courses overlap or supplies fall within 60 days of each other and no Group F stomach protection is supplied for that period. Assess two or more bleeding-risk groups under F2 regardless of protection. If this medicine pattern qualifies and age during the combination is missing, report only a possible finding, name the missing fact as Age and ask the pharmacist for the age in years at that time. A confirmed age below 65 excludes this episode. Count each aspirin supply once. If its purpose is unclear, check both possible uses for that course. If both give one unprotected group, report F1. If both give two or more groups, assess F2. If only one gives F1, report only a possible F1 finding, cite the aspirin supply and ask the pharmacist whether that aspirin was used for clot prevention or for pain or inflammation during that course. For an F1 finding, ask the patient whether they used any stomach-protecting or acid-lowering medicine during the same period, including products bought without a prescription or supplied by a hospital or another pharmacy, and if so which product, dose and timing. Before contacting the GP, have the pharmacist consider that answer and any H2 blocker in the record or reported by the patient, and decide whether an H2 blocker provided adequate protection.
cannot_be_seen: Medicines bought without a prescription or supplied by another pharmacy or hospital may be missing, including aspirin, NSAIDs and stomach protection. The supplies alone do not show what was taken or a history of ulcers or bleeding.
ask_the_gp: A review of whether both medicines are still needed and whether stomach protection is advisable.
